SA.name: Saudi Arabia
SA.summary: Still the hardest-hit Gulf country: Riyadh is partially reopened and some airlines are returning, but several suspensions continue.

news.t: Riyadh Air restarts Riyadh–Dubai and Riyadh–Manila flights from 22 November, with Jakarta from 23 November.
Yemen’s Houthis warned airlines to avoid Saudi airspace and threatened more attacks on infrastructure.
Etihad has extended its Abu Dhabi–Riyadh and Abu Dhabi–Dammam cancellations to 30 November.
flydubai has suspended Riyadh and Abha flights until 27 November.

airports.name: King Khalid International
airports.info: Partially reopened, with limited domestic and international flights.

airports.name: King Abdulaziz International
airports.info: Main gateway for Hajj and Umrah, and a Saudia hub. Still operating.

airports.name: King Fahd International
airports.info: Serves the Eastern Province. Several airlines have paused flights here.

AE.name: United Arab Emirates
AE.summary: Airports are open, but the UAE is inside Europe’s Gulf conflict-zone advisory and Saudi routes are reduced.

news.t: Riyadh Air is flying Riyadh–Dubai twice daily again from 22 November.
Dubai International handled 50.4 million passengers in the first nine months of 2026, down 28.1% on last year.
EASA’s conflict-zone advisory covering the UAE now runs until 31 January 2027.
Emirates, flydubai and Air Arabia are running selected services to Saudi Arabia.

airports.name: Dubai International
airports.info: One of the world’s busiest international airports and the Emirates hub.

airports.name: Al Maktoum International
airports.info: Dubai’s second airport and a major private-jet hub.

QA.name: Qatar
QA.summary: Flights are operating normally from Doha, under Europe’s Gulf conflict-zone advisory.

news.t: Qatar Airways has restarted daily flights to Riyadh and Dammam.
EASA’s Gulf advisory covering Qatar is extended to 31 January 2027.

airports.name: Hamad International
airports.info: Qatar’s main airport and the Qatar Airways hub.

airports.name: Doha International
airports.info: The original Doha airport, now used for limited and special flights.

BH.name: Bahrain
BH.summary: Bahrain International is operating, and Gulf Air has restarted Riyadh flights. Europe’s Gulf advisory still applies.

news.t: Gulf Air has resumed operations at Riyadh Airport.
EASA’s Gulf advisory covering Bahrain is extended to 31 January 2027.

airports.name: Bahrain International
airports.info: The country’s only civil airport and the Gulf Air hub.

KW.name: Kuwait
KW.summary: Kuwait International is open. Kuwait is covered by Europe’s Gulf conflict-zone advisory.

news.t: EASA’s Gulf advisory covering Kuwait is extended to 31 January 2027.

airports.name: Kuwait International
airports.info: The country’s only civil airport and the Kuwait Airways hub.

OM.name: Oman
OM.summary: Omani airports are operating, under Europe’s conflict-zone advisory for the Gulf and Gulf of Oman.

news.t: EASA’s advisory for the Gulf of Oman and Omani airspace is extended to 31 January 2027.

airports.name: Muscat International
airports.info: Oman’s main airport and the Oman Air hub.

airports.name: Salalah
airports.info: Gateway to the south, busiest in the summer khareef season.

airports.name: Duqm International
airports.info: A newer airport serving the Duqm economic zone.
